newsitem.title: USA: FTC Staples ruling bad for whole sector--analysts.
newsitem.headline: FTC Staples ruling bad for whole sector--analysts.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission's rejection of the $4 billion merger of Staples Inc and Office Depot is a bad sign for the office supplies sector and possibly the entire retail industry, anaylsts said.
"It's not good for Staples; it's certainly not good for Office Depot. But much more than that, it's bad for the sector and retail in general," PaineWebber analyst Aram Rubinson said.
Office Depot was off 6-3/8 at 12-3/4 following news of the FTC decision. Staples was up one at 22-1/4.

"There's a lot of over-capacity in the retail sector and if the government is not going to let these kinds of mergers go through, it condemns retail to over-capacity forever," said Rubinson, who had a neutral rating on Office Depot and a buy on Staples.
Sanford Bernstein's Ursula Moran said that "any analyst who has a buy on Office Depot -- and I do -- has got to be disappointed by this (FTC) decision."
Moran, who also has a buy on Staples, said the decision will cause her to reevaluate both ratings.
"It will absolutely cause me to do an evalution of what the future looks like for both companies," she said.

Standard & Poors Corp analyst Michael Pizzi, who has a buy rating on Staples and a hold on Office Depot, said, "I'm surprised by the decision, particularly after the sale of the 63 stores to Office Max. I thought that would satisfy the FTC's opposition."
Pizzi said he doubted the companies would go to court against the FTC.
"The other option is to abandon the deal," he said.
"While they might win in court, it could take a couple years. Perhaps that wouldn't be prudent," he added.
